solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Displays reason for playing area

parts.note: to sport something is to display or show it off, so displays is sports
grounds are reasons or justification, as in grounds for complaint

explanation.surface: Someone justifies a playing area by pointing to what it shows off.
explanation.definitionFit: A sportsground is a field or stadium laid out for games and athletics.

clue.text: New version of map, I grant, reveals bird

indicators.note: a new version reworks the letters that follow into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A revised map, with the speaker's permission, shows where a bird lives.
explanation.definitionFit: The ptarmigan is a grouse of mountain and Arctic regions that turns white in winter.

clue.text: Recording showing relative simplicity

parts.note: ease means simplicity, the absence of difficulty

explanation.surface: A record that shows how easy a relative finds things.
explanation.definitionFit: A new release is a record or film issued to the public, so a recording put out for sale.

clue.text: Tennyson, losing heart, junked poem

indicators.note: junked suggests the remaining letters are scrapped and rebuilt into another order
the heart of an eight-letter name is its central pair of letters, which is dropped here

explanation.surface: Tennyson, dispirited, threw away one of his poems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' removes NY, the middle two letters of TENNYSON, leaving TENSON; 'junked' then rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonnet is a fourteen-line verse form, one particular kind of poem.

clue.text: Control quantity of furniture in store

indicators.note: only a quantity, a portion, of the following words is taken, the letters lying across them

explanation.surface: Managing how much furniture is held in a warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'furniture', all of 'in' and the start of 'store'.
explanation.definitionFit: Reins are the straps that guide a horse, and figuratively the means of control, as in 'take the reins'.

clue.text: European chasing American employment

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so the European piece comes after the American one

parts.note: US stands for United States, hence American

explanation.surface: A European job-hunter follows an American in search of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Use and employment are synonyms: putting something to work for a purpose.

clue.text: Start to drain river — modified dam lower? A fantastic vision

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is used

parts.note: R is the usual map abbreviation for river

indicators.note: modified means changed, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Engineering instructions: drain the river and lower an altered dam, all a fanciful scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamworld is an imagined place of fantasy, unrelated to reality.

clue.text: Biblical figure starts to pray at undue length

indicators.note: the starts of these four words are their initial letters, read in order

explanation.surface: Someone from scripture launches into a prayer that goes on far too long.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul the Apostle, writer of many New Testament epistles, is a leading figure of the Bible.

clue.text: Innocence of Scot's refusal to accommodate one old soldier

indicators.note: to accommodate is to house, so the refusal holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: nae is Scots for no
I is the Roman numeral for one
VET is short for veteran, an old soldier

explanation.surface: A Scot innocently refuses to put up a veteran.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is a lack of worldly experience, an artless innocence.

clue.text: Reminder to include heathen article for indoctrination?

indicators.note: including means taking inside, so the nudge goes round the heathen word

parts.note: a prod is a nudge or prompt, a reminder
a pagan is a heathen
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A prompt to bring a heathen tract into a campaign of indoctrination.
explanation.definitionFit: Propaganda is biased material spread to instil a doctrine, the instrument of indoctrination.

clue.text: Go wild with anger about current unit

indicators.note: about means around, so the anger word wraps the unit

parts.note: rage is fierce anger
the amp is the unit of electric current

explanation.surface: Someone loses control, furious about the electricity tariff.
explanation.definitionFit: To rampage is to rush about violently and destructively, running riot.

clue.text: Limits to some curious immunising agent

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its outermost letters, first and last

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or curious

explanation.surface: A cautious remark about the boundaries of some odd vaccine.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum here is the old British adjective meaning strange, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A serum is blood fluid carrying antibodies, injected to give immunity.

clue.text: Electrical device runs: fierce with it, possibly

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: possibly signals that these letters might be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A machine described as running fiercely, maybe.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectifier converts alternating current to direct current, a component in power supplies.

clue.text: Small animal breaking leg in excavation

indicators.note: in places the broken letters inside the hole

parts.note: a pit is a hole dug out, an excavation

indicators.note: breaking smashes the word leg so its letters reform in a new order

explanation.surface: A little creature breaks its leg after falling into a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A piglet is a young pig, a small farm animal.

clue.text: Hitchcock film: hard copy's edited

indicators.note: edited means revised, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
taken as written, the letters of copys

explanation.surface: A hard copy of a Hitchcock screenplay has been edited.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Hitchcock's 1960 thriller, famous for its shower scene, bears this title.

clue.text: Reduced volume covering question over British entertainment industry

indicators.note: covering means going around, so the shortened word encloses the rest
reduced means cut short, so the final letter is lopped off

parts.note: size is volume, how much space something takes up

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means placed above, so the question comes before the British letter

parts.note: how is a question word

explanation.surface: Turning down the volume over a question about British show business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduced volume' reads like turning the sound down, but volume here means size, and only its last letter is cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Showbiz is informal for show business, the world of film, theatre and television.

clue.text: Outmoded dictionary location of "item"

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., too old to be any use
second meaning: in alphabetical order the word item comes just after the word it, so it sits beyond that entry

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is cryptic: in a dictionary 'item' is filed after 'it' because it starts with those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Past it is an idiom for someone or something no longer capable, worn out by age.

clue.text: Clever person dismissing one classification

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a genius is an exceptionally clever person
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A brilliant person dismisses one way of sorting things.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a genus is a taxonomic rank between family and species.

clue.text: Perfume deception taking in millions

indicators.note: taking in means holding inside, so the deception encloses the letter

parts.note: a sell is a hoax or deception, as in 'what a sell'
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A scam over a perfume that rakes in millions.
explanation.definitionFit: Smell can mean scent or fragrance, so it serves as a noun for a perfume.

clue.text: Spies blocking a single performance mostly unfriendly

indicators.note: blocking means sitting in the way, so the agency goes inside
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a solo is a performance by one person
the CIA is the US intelligence agency, a body of spies

explanation.surface: Secret agents interrupt a one-man show, rather rudely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a single performance' splits into the article A plus a solo; 'mostly' trims only the solo before the spies go in.
explanation.definitionFit: Asocial describes someone avoiding company, lacking interest in others.

clue.text: Ignore info returned by the French court

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the slang word is read backwards

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Information is sent back by a French court and disregarded.
explanation.definitionFit: To neglect is to fail to attend to something, disregarding it.

clue.text: Slit releasing hydrogen or helium?

indicators.note: releasing lets go of the letter, so it is removed

parts.note: a gash is a long cut or slit
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: A cut lets out hydrogen, or possibly helium, from a balloon.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks helium as an example of the answer rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Helium is a noble element that is a vapour at room temperature, one example of the category.

clue.text: Provide temptation for one coming in to play cricket

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so the numeral goes inside

parts.note: to bat is to take a turn as batsman in cricket
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Luring someone to come in and join a cricket game.
explanation.definitionFit: To bait is to lure, setting out something enticing to draw a target in.

clue.text: Unconditional love? There's no warmth here

parts.note: absolute means total, without condition
love is zero in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: Devotion with no strings attached, yet a cold heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' points to romance, but in tennis it means nil.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute zero is minus 273.15 Celsius, the lowest possible temperature, at which molecules hold no heat energy.
